question: For a closed path, $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l}=0$. Does this always mean that the magnetic field is zero at every point on the path? Explain with reason using Ampere’s circuital law.

options.A: No. By Ampere’s law, $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l=\mu_0I_{\text{enclosed}}=0$ means the net enclosed current is zero. The magnetic field can still be non-zero at points on the path due to external currents or cancelling enclosed currents.
options.B: Yes. A zero line integral proves $\vec B=0$ at every point on the path.
options.C: Yes. A zero line integral means there are no currents anywhere near the path.
options.D: No. It means the magnetic field must be constant and parallel to the path.
